results: 1. anticipatory jerk to a feigned tendon-hammer approach (Hallett sign): POSITIVE - the jerk occurs when the hammer is stopped just short of the tendon, provoked by the visual stimulus alone
2. back-averaged EEG for a Bereitschaftspotential before the movements: Bereitschaftspotential present before the jerks
3. somatosensory evoked potentials (giant SEP, C-reflex): normal, no giant SEP and no C-reflex - excludes cortical reflex myoclonus
4. jerk latency and burst-duration measurement: long and VARIABLE latency with a long duration of muscle contraction - the pattern of voluntary movement, not of cortical myoclonus
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Functional (psychogenic) myoclonus of the leg, consistent with a functional neurological symptom disorder (conversion disorder).

ALTERNATIVES:
1. Tics (simple motor tic of the leg) - though typically shorter and suppressible
2. Spinal segmental myoclonus - less likely given Bereitschaftspotential present and variable latency
3. Functional dystonia with myoclonic tremor - related functional movement disorder phenotype
